post.description:
Upserts a contact in the organization the API key belongs to. Send an email, a phone, or both.

With an email, the email is the key, matched without regard to case. A phone sent with it is
stored as an extra phone of that contact.

With no email, the phone alone is the key. It must start with + and a country code. Iris
updates the one active contact that holds the number, or creates a contact when none does when the credential can reach it.
When more than one contact holds it, the call writes nothing. For a 409, find them with
`contacts_find_by_endpoint` and update one with `contacts_update`. When no active contact holds
it and an archived contact has it as its main phone, the call answers 409 and writes nothing:
restore that contact with `contacts_restore`. An archived contact never matches otherwise.

A credential that reaches no location gets 403 `insufficient_role` before any lookup, even when the email or phone exists.
A match outside the key's reach (its location scope or own-records limit) answers 404, as a missing contact does, before any write.
With no email, a reach-limited key gets 404 if any phone holder is outside its reach. It gets 409 for several holders only when all are reachable.
The holder reach check covers every holder in one database call.
A contact outside the key's reach answers 404 even when this key created it.
For a location key, a concurrent create of the same contact at the caller's location merges into that contact.
An own-records key gets 404 until an existing contact is the member's client.
An unknown email or phone creates a contact only when the credential can reach it. An unknown email still answers differently from a known one outside reach. This is the same existence signal Zapier upsert gives (IRIS-7115).

Only contacts this call creates get a location link. Matched contacts keep their links.
Send optional `location_id` within the key scope and organization, or receive 403 `insufficient_role`.
A key with one location implies it. Several locations require `location_id` on creation, or 400 `location_id_required`.
An explicit inactive location answers 400 `location_inactive` on creation. A sole implied location that is inactive or deleted answers 400 `location_inactive` on creation.
Organization-wide keys without `location_id` create unlinked.
A create and its location link are one write. A failed link leaves no contact and answers the error 400 `location_inactive`. A retry gets the same answer until the location is active again.

A new contact must be one the credential can reach, or the call writes nothing.
An own-records credential gets 403 `insufficient_role` for a new email or phone. An existing client still merges.
Both 403 refusals say `This credential cannot reach the contact it would create`. With no location, ask an owner or admin to give the holder a location. With own records, ask someone with wider access to create the contact.
The 400 `location_inactive` for a credential with one location names that location, not a `location_id` the caller sent. Another `location_id` answers 403. Ask for the location to be made active.
The same credential gets the same answer until the holder's locations, the location's status or the contact changes. `me_get` shows the holder's current role and locations.
The no-location 403 comes first. The own-records 403 comes after the lookup and before field and stage checks. The sole-location 400 comes after field, stage and location checks.
A matched contact that is gone at write time answers 404 and creates nothing. An active phone holder archived during the call answers 404, and a retry gets the 409.

A stage value in `fields` must be a pipeline stage string. Empty strings and null clear it. Whitespace-only strings clear it and are stored as an empty string.
Changing the stage on an existing contact fires `stage_changed` automations and the
`crm.contact.stage_changed` event. A new contact fires only lead-created automations.

`cancel_events` are processed first, then `events` are fired, so one request can replace
the journey a contact is on. Cancellations and other events are best effort.
`assessment_abandoned` requires transactional acceptance: failures fail the request even if
the contact was already upserted. Only a matching `assessmentAbandonment` receipt with
`status: accepted` confirms durable enrollment acceptance; delivery is not guaranteed.
An event whose name no active sequence subscribes to leaves its `key` unspent, so a later
retry still enrolls.

`skip_automations: true` makes the upsert itself start nothing: no "New lead" sequence, no
`crm.lead.created`, `crm.contact.updated` or `crm.contact.stage_changed` event, or stage-change automation.
Named `events` and `cancel_events` still run.

With an API key, an upsert that creates the contact confirms its email: the AI agents may then email it model-written text. An upsert that matches an existing contact confirms nothing. Use `contacts_update` to confirm its email. A call with an OAuth token, or one made through `/api/v1/mcp`, confirms nothing.
external_sync keeps token-loss outages as disconnected with their last sync time. Retired bindings are omitted.

400.description: Invalid request body, neither email nor valid phone, non-string stage, unknown pipeline stage in `fields` or a live stage field with no options, `location_id_required` for creation with several locations, `location_inactive` for an explicit inactive location on creation, `location_inactive` for a credential's sole location when it is inactive or deleted, or `location_inactive` for a raced create-time link

401.description: Missing, malformed, unknown, revoked or expired API key

403.description:
`field_not_editable`, or `insufficient_role` with message `Location access denied` for a location outside the key scope or organization. `insufficient_role` with message `This credential cannot reach the contact it would create` when the credential reaches no location, or is limited to its own records and the contact is new

409.description: `stage_config_changed`: the live stage key changed and `fields` includes the new key. Retry the request. Also returned when no email was sent and multiple reachable contacts hold the phone, or an archived reachable contact has it as its main phone.

get.description:
Finds contacts in the key’s organization. Send at most one filter:

- `q`: free text, matched against name, email and phone, without regard to case.
- `email`: the exact email, without regard to case. Returns at most one contact.
- `phone`: the exact phone number. Returns at most one contact.

Archived contacts are hidden from every search. With no filter, lists active contacts, most recently seen first.
A member’s credential finds only contacts linked to its locations. A MEMBER at the own-records level
finds only the clients of their own appointments.

A MEMBER, and a MANAGER without the contacts power, get each contact’s `id`, `name`, `email` and
`phone` only, listed by name. A MANAGER with the power gets whole contacts, as an owner does.
A predicate on a denied field answers 422 `field_not_searchable`; free text matches viewable fields only.
external_sync keeps token-loss outages as disconnected with their last sync time. Retired bindings are omitted.

post.description:
Cancels a PENDING or EXPIRED invitation and invites the same email again, in the same role.
The person gets a new email with a new link, valid for 7 days, and the old link stops working.
Answers the new invitation, which has a new `id`. Use it when the person lost the email, the
invitation expired, or `invitations_create` answered 409 for a PENDING invitation.
An OWNER or ADMIN calls it. A MEMBER’s or MANAGER’s credential gets 403 `insufficient_role`, as in the dashboard.
An organization key gets 403 `no_acting_user`. 404 `not_found`: no PENDING or EXPIRED invitation with that id.
409 `ROLE_NOT_RESENDABLE`: the invitation holds a role other than ADMIN or MEMBER. Revoke it and create a new one.

500 `UNKNOWN_ERROR`: the email could not be sent. Iris then tries to restore the old invitation, as best effort only. The old one can stay cancelled, with the unsent new one PENDING or with no pending invitation for the email. Call `invitations_list` after a failed resend to see what is pending.

Switching between select_all and an explicit list is a changed request and also answers 409. While staff approval is pending, an unchanged retry answers 202 again. The public, versioned API of Iris. Authenticate with an API key:
`Authorization: Bearer iris_sk_…`. An owner or admin mints organization keys under
Organization → API keys, and any member mints personal keys under My agent access. Keys carry
scopes; a key without a route’s scope gets a 403 with `{ "error": "insufficient_scope" }`.
Each operation’s `x-iris-scope` names the scope it needs, or is null when any live key may call it.

Agent clients that cannot hold a key (Claude Desktop, claude.ai, ChatGPT) use OAuth 2.1 with
PKCE instead. They discover the authorization server from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`,
and send the access token the same way. Its scopes are the scopes above.

An OAuth token acts for the person who granted it, and a personal key for its owner. That
person’s current role and locations cap it. An owner or admin can turn a person’s agent access
off, alone or by role: their personal keys and OAuth tokens then get the 401 until it is back on.
Each operation’s `x-member-access` states its access mode. Resource operations use `action`:
`x-iris-action` names the SQL permission checked in request mode for the current principal.
Denied actions return 403 with the SQL reason and approval count. Required approval does not execute,
except where `x-iris-approval` says so: `file` files the approval request (202) and `execute` runs an approved one.
`x-iris-sms-setting` adds the existing SMS eligibility check. Open introspection remains `open`.
`me_get` shows the person, role and locations behind the credential. Record and tenant bounds still apply.

Every path is versioned. `v1` only ever grows: a breaking change ships as `v2`, and the
old version keeps serving with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers until it is retired.

idempotency_key.description: Your own key for this send. The stored answer replays for 24 hours without sending again. For those 24 hours a changed request answers 409 `idempotency_key_reused`, including while approval is pending and after it. After that, a same-key retry of a completed send replays while resolved recipients stay the same. Changed recipients or select_all mode answer 409 `idempotency_conflict`. While staff approval is pending, an unchanged retry answers 202. After approval, changed approval material can answer 403 `approval_denied`.

subject_kind.description: Accepts document, hold, package, or subscription_signup. Package and signup links require plan_kind, plan_id, currency and bill_to_contact_id. They need an OWNER or ADMIN credential, or one acting on behalf of one. Hold deposits use card only.

subject_id.description: The subject ID. Document and hold links require it. Package and subscription_signup links take plan_id instead. For package and subscription_signup links it must equal plan_id. For holds, use the live deposit-gated hold ID. A hold with mixed currencies answers 422 hold_not_payable.

allow_bank_debit.description: For invoice links, omit this field to derive eligibility from the account switch and Stripe ach_debit_payments capability. An explicit true requires both; holds always use card only. Package and signup links use card only. An explicit true answers 400 bank_debit_not_available. The stored value is frozen on the payment attempt.

idempotency_key.description: Organization-wide retry key for MCP or REST. REST also accepts Idempotency-Key. If both are supplied, they must match. Replays recheck access and return the same URL. Changed fields answer 409 idempotency_conflict. Omit the key to create a distinct intent with a stored server key for later sending. Without a caller key, the original create request cannot be replayed.

document_id.description: The invoice ID for document links, or the current purchase draft for package and subscription_signup links. Null before first open and for hold deposit links.

url.description: The copy URL, returned only by create and its idempotent replay.

payment_started_at.description: When the settling payment started, from Checkout completion or receipt-sourced processing evidence. Present only with existing_link_id.

bill_to_group_id.description: The group billed. Give this or `bill_to_contact_id`, not both.

quantity.description: How many of the plan each period bills and grants.

currency.description: The currency, fixed for the life of the subscription. Defaults to the organization currency.

location_id.description: The location the subscription belongs to.

starts_at.description: When period 1 starts. Defaults to now.

auto_issue.description: Issue each period invoice when the period opens.

auto_send.description: Send each issued period invoice to its remembered recipients.

credit_terms.description: Explicit credit terms: each period funds its grant when it opens instead of when its invoice is paid.

issuer.description: Defaults to `iris`. `stripe` makes Stripe issue and collect each invoice on the connected account. It needs an active Stripe connection and a contact bill-to, and refuses credit terms, a future `starts_at`, `auto_issue` false, `auto_send` true and a plan with default tax rates. The subscription stays pending, with no Iris period or invoice, until its first Stripe invoice is paid.

period.description: The created billing period. Its price follows financial access. Null for a scheduled resume or a withdrawn pause.

change.description: The scheduled or applied change. Adjustment amounts follow financial access. Null for a withdrawn pause.

adjustment_document_id.description: The adjustment invoice or credit note. An invoice can remain draft when auto-issue is disabled or refused.

timing.description: `period_end` stops renewal at the next boundary. `immediate` cancels now and needs the business setting `immediate_cancel_allowed`. Neither credits anything.

On a Stripe-issued subscription, a next_period change stays scheduled. Iris shows the old plan and seats until Stripe switches the phase at the period end. Omitted timing also uses next_period, with no proration or extra invoice. A new next-period change on a Stripe subscription replaces any pending one. Immediate prorates the paid item and releases the pending schedule. Stripe on_date stays refused (R6).

effective_at.description: Required for on_date, within the current period. Stripe-issued subscriptions refuse on_date (R6).

old_amount_minor.description: Current period amount in minor units. Visible to billing readers only.

new_amount_minor.description: Changed period amount in minor units. Visible to billing readers only.

adjustment_minor.description: Signed charge or credit in minor units, rounded once. It includes tax when adjustment_excludes_tax is false. Visible to billing readers only.

adjustment_excludes_tax.description: True when adjustment_minor excludes tax. False when the organization's prices include tax.

extra_units.description: Signed floor of prorated unit difference. Positive units wait for adjustment payment. Negative units remove no grant.
